area: F4 Branch and bound (cycle B, oracles first)

findings.title: Rounded near-integral LP solution becomes the incumbent without a feasibility check: .optimal at an infeasible point
findings.claim: Status.swift:5: '.optimal: An optimal solution was found and proven (within the gap, for MILP)'. README §4 Limits 'Results': 'Optimal' means 'feasible and dual feasible to 1e-7'. README §3 risk 1 names CompiledLP.maxViolation(at:) as the way to check a point. README §2.4: primal holds the n values of the solution.
findings.observed:
Model: max y - 1000z s.t. y - 1e6 z <= 0, y in [0, 0.4], z binary. BranchAndBound() parallel, Simplex(.dual) deterministic, Gap(relative: 0, absolute: 0) and Automatic all return status=optimal objective=0.3996 bound=0.3996 x=(z=0, y=0.4) nodes=1. maxViolation gives rows 0.4, and objective(at: x)=0.4, not 0.3996. The exact optimum is 0 at (0, 0). M=1e7 gives 0.39996. M=1e5 is correct, because z=4e-6 is branched on.

Second model: max x1+x2 s.t. 1e6 x1 - 1e6 x2 <= -0.5, binaries. Every engine and Automatic return optimal 1.9999995 at (1, 1), with objective(at: x)=2.0 and the row violated by 0.5. The exact optimum is 1 at (0, 1).
findings.whyWrong:
The root LP vertex has z=4e-7, which is inside the 1e-6 integrality tolerance, so expand() treats the LP solution as integral. It rounds the integer columns and offers the rounded point with the LP objective. It never calls isFeasible on that point and never recomputes the objective, although the rounding and diving heuristics do both.

Rounding a column with coefficient 1e6 moves the row activity by 0.4. The returned point therefore violates its row by 0.4, which is 4e6 times primalFeasibility and fails under any absolute or relative reading. The reported objective is attained by no feasible point.

Any LP vertex is exposed when an integer column is near-integral but not exact and has large row coefficients. Big-M rows y <= M z with M above 1e6 times the range of y are the common case.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/TreeSearch.swift:200-203. In expand(), when fractional.isEmpty, the integer columns are rounded and offer(objective: objective, x: solution) is called with the LP objective, with no isFeasible and no objective recompute.

findings.title: Incumbent keeps the inflated LP objective, so the objective-step cutoff prunes the true optimum: .optimal a full unit below it, even with Gap(0,0)
findings.claim: Status.swift:5: '.optimal ... proven (within the gap, for MILP)'. README §3 risk 10: '.optimal means incumbent - bound <= max(1e-6, 1e-4*max(1, abs(incumbent)))', with the mitigation 'Pass a tighter Gap to BranchAndBound when the exact optimum matters'. README §1 promises 'a proven bound'.
findings.observed:
Minimized model, from F4 minimize 766: max 2x0+21x1+x2+24x3+3x4+22x5+7x6+11x7+9x8, x binary, subject to:
- 2x0+7x1+5x2+4x3+9x4+2x5+4x6+8x7 <= 21
- 1e6x1-1e6x2 <= 0.7381787698023262
- 1e6x1-1e6x6 <= 0.8789166025652512
- -1e6x4+1e6x8 <= 0.6272604256811957

BranchAndBound() (parallel and deterministic), Gap(relative: 0, absolute: 0) and the Simplex(.dual) engine all return status=optimal objective=66.00000564534383 bound=66.00000564534383 at x=(1,0,0,1,0,1,1,1,0), whose value is 66. The exact optimum is 67 at (1,0,0,1,1,1,1,0,1): row 1 gives 21 <= 21 and the other rows give 0, -1e6 and 0. This was checked by enumeration and by hand.

The unminimized 11-variable instance nearint2#766 (F4 step 766) returns 72.00000564534383 against the true 73 from default-par, default-det, Gap(0,0)-det and Automatic. In a random family (8 to 11 binaries, knapsack rows, linking rows 1e6 d - 1e6 e <= delta), 3,000 seeds x 13 configs produced 91 results beyond the gap.
findings.whyWrong:
The LP-path incumbent is stored with the LP objective V+E, while the point's own value is V. Here E is 5.6e-6, gained by near-integral columns exploiting the fractional rhs of the 1e6-scaled rows.

All costs are integral, so objectiveStep=1 and the cutoff is incumbent - 1 + 1e-9*max(1, |incumbent|). That formula assumes the incumbent lies on the objective lattice. Since E > 1e-9*|inc|, a node whose LP bound is exactly V+1 lies above the cutoff and is pruned, although it contains the solution of value V+1. The search then completes, and BranchAndBound reports bound = incumbent.

The result misses the optimum by 1.0, against a slack of 0.0066, or 0 under Gap(0,0). Both the status and the bound are false.

Two mechanism checks support this. Adding a fixed continuous column with a cost (objectiveStep 0) makes the search find 73. Dividing the row shifts by 1000, which puts E below 1e-9 relative, also finds 73.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/TreeSearch.swift:200-203 offers the LP objective for the rounded point. The step cutoffs at TreeSearch.swift:83-87 (cutoff(for:)) and SearchTree.swift:312-317 (cutoff) allow only 1e-9 relative. BranchAndBound.swift:350-352 sets bound = incumbent on .complete.

findings.title: With objective step 0, the reported 'proven' bound lies below the true optimum and gap reads 0 (slack-pruned nodes never reach prunedBound; .complete overwrites the bound)
findings.claim: README §1: results carry 'a proven bound'. Analysis.swift:22: 'Proven bound'. The README §3 risk 3 mitigation: 'read bound and BranchAndBoundAnalysis.gap to know how far the incumbent may be from the optimum'. SearchTree.swift:171-172: prunedBound is 'The bound of nodes that were pruned or dropped without being fully explored; the proven bound can never exceed it'.
findings.observed:
(1) max 10000x0 + 3.31234567xa + 2xb + 2xc s.t. 3xa+2xb+2xc <= 4, binaries. BranchAndBound(), parallel and deterministic, returns status=optimal objective=10003.31234567 bound=10003.31234567 gap=0.0 nodes=1. Yet x=(1,0,1,1) is feasible with value 10004, and the root LP bound is 10004.31234567. With p=3.3 (objective step 0.1) the same search reports the valid bound 10004.3.

(2) The package's own generator, InstanceGenerator.randomMILP(rows: 6, columns: 30, seed: 13, integerFraction: 0.8, upper: 2, integralData: false), with BranchAndBound() and with deterministic: optimal 696.8528577299143, bound equal, gap 0.0. A feasible integral point has 696.8684768970606 (row violation 2.8e-14). Seeds 18 and 21 behave the same.

(3) randomMILP(rows: 12, columns: 60, seed: 4242, upper: 1, integralData: false) with Gap(relative: 0.2): optimal 523.2299614429742, bound equal, gap 0.0, while the optimum is 586.8790317749188. The bound is 10.8% below the optimum.

.boundImproved events carry the same invalid values.
findings.whyWrong:
For a maximization, a proven bound must be at least every feasible objective, and the gap must bound the distance to the optimum. With objectiveStep == 0 the cutoff is incumbent - gap slack.

TreeSearch discards nodes whose bound lies in [incumbent - slack, incumbent) in four places:
- process(): node.bound >= cut;
- the engine's .cutoff outcome;
- objective >= currentCutoff(), checked twice.
None of these tells SearchTree, so prunedBound never sees the nodes. On CloseReason.complete, BranchAndBound then replaces the bound with the incumbent.

The status is still within the gap, but the bound and gap fields assert an exactness that is false. A user following the risk 3 mitigation reads gap 0 for an incumbent 10.8% from the optimum. Any model with a continuous column that has a cost, or with non-integral costs, is exposed.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/BranchAndBound.swift:350-352 (case .complete: if hasIncumbent { boundValue = incumbent.objective }). TreeSearch.swift:139, 154, 177 and 214 discard nodes against the slack cutoff without telling the tree. SearchTree.swift:340, 359 and 377 feed prunedBound only from push, pop and removeBestBound. provenBound is at SearchTree.swift:402-404.

findings.title: Rounding and diving incumbents pass an unscaled 1e-7*(1+|rhs|) feasibility test: .optimal above the solver's own LP relaxation on badly scaled rows
findings.claim: README §2.3: Tolerances.primalFeasibility is 1e-7. README §4 Limits 'Results': 'feasible ... to 1e-7'. An integer solution can never beat its own LP relaxation.
findings.observed:
(1) max x+y s.t. 1e-7x + 1e-7y <= 1.5e-7, x and y binary. Every engine returns status=optimal objective=2.0 bound=2.0 at x=(1,1), from the incumbent '2.0@0/rounding'. The root LP is 1.5, and the exact optimum is 1.

(2) max x s.t. 3x + y <= 1e9+1, x integer in [0, 1e9], y fixed 0. The result is optimal 333333334 with bound 333333334. The row activity is 1000000002 > 1000000001, and the absolute maxViolation is 1.0. The root LP is 333333333.667, and the exact optimum is 333333333.

BranchAndBound(heuristics: .none) returns the exact optima, 1 and 333333333.
findings.whyWrong:
TreeSearch.isFeasible works on the unscaled problem with the allowance feasibility*(1+|bound|).
- On a row whose coefficients are 1e-7, that allowance is an absolute 1e-7, a 33% violation in the row's own units. The LP engine works on the scaled problem and rejects the point.
- On a row with rhs 1e9, it is 100 units, which admits a whole unit of integer data.

The search then closes with an incumbent above the root relaxation bound that the same solver computed, and reports bound = incumbent.

Under a relative-tolerance reading, as SCIP uses, both points are within tolerance, and the README does not say whether the tolerance is absolute or relative. That is why this is graded medium, not critical. The incumbent beating the LP bound is still an internal inconsistency.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/TreeSearch.swift:325-340 (isFeasible: the column test at line 328 and the row test at line 335), used by the rounding heuristic and by dive().

findings.title: deterministic: true gives a different search with threads = 1 than with threads >= 2
findings.claim: README §3 risk 8: 'deterministic: true on BranchAndBound and CPSAT runs a single worker with a fixed seed'. README §4 Limits: 'Parallel search is not reproducible unless deterministic: true, which uses one worker'. Read together, these say the result does not depend on SolveContext.threads.
findings.observed: On misc03, deterministic with threads=1 takes 559 nodes and returns 3359.9999999999995. With threads 2, 3, 4, 8 and 16 it takes 1293 nodes and returns 3360.0, identically across those thread counts. On p0033 the counts are 1575 and 1605 nodes. Each thread count is reproducible run to run.
findings.whyWrong:
runProbes runs the strong-branching and pseudocost probes inline on the worker's engine when the ConcurrencyBudget grants no slot, as with threads=1. Otherwise it runs them on fresh engines in child tasks. That changes the probe results and therefore the tree.

resolvedThreads defaults to activeProcessorCount, so a 'deterministic' run on a 1-core container differs from one on a laptop. The package's determinism test pins threads = 4, so it cannot see this.

Objectives agree to within 1 ulp, so this affects reproducibility, not correctness.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/TreeSearch.swift:581-597. runProbes calls budget.borrow; when extra == 0 the probes run inline on the worker engine. The test pin is at Tests/ZTronLPBranchAndBoundTests/BranchAndBoundTests.swift:301 (context.threads = 4).

findings.title: A nodeLimit equal to the node count of the complete search reports .feasible(nodeLimit) although the search proved optimality
findings.claim: Status.swift: '.feasible(stoppedBy:): An incumbent exists; optimality was not proven'.
findings.observed: p0033, deterministic: the complete search takes 1605 nodes. nodeLimit 1605 returns feasible(nodeLimit) with objective 3089 and bound 3089 (gap 0), and nodeLimit 1606 returns optimal. misc03 behaves the same at 1293.
findings.whyWrong: SearchTree.absorb closes with .nodeLimit as soon as nodesProcessed reaches the limit, before next() can observe that no open node is left. A search that finished and proved optimality (bound == incumbent) is reported as stopped by a limit. This is conservative, with no false .optimal or .infeasible, but the status understates the result.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/SearchTree.swift:249 (in absorb: if let limit = nodeLimit, nodesProcessed >= limit, !closed { close(.nodeLimit) })

findings.title: lpIterations counts each strong-branching probe as a fixed share of the probe cap rather than the pivots it took; the README §5 'LP pivots' columns inherit the synthetic count
findings.claim: README §5 MIP table: the 'LP pivots' columns, and 'The primal node engine, the default, takes between 0.60 and 1.65 times the LP pivots of the dual one'. BranchAndBoundAnalysis.lpIterations.
findings.observed: runProbes returns candidates.count * 2 * limit / 4 as the iteration count of its probes, whether they run inline or in parallel and whatever they actually took. With probeIterationLimit 50, that is 25 pivots per candidate (12.5 per probe).

claimsHeld.claim: MILP optimality against exhaustive enumeration on small random models, over 13 configurations. Models: binary; general integer with negative, asymmetric and fractional bounds; mixed with up to 3 continuous columns (vertex-enumeration LP oracle); equality rows; parity-infeasible; free integer. Configurations: primal, dual and IPM engines, deterministic and parallel, presolve on and off, full presolve plus postsolve, mostFractional+DFS+no heuristics, strong+bestBound, Gap(0,0), threads=1. Checked: the status, the objective within the gap and never better than the optimum, the primal integral and feasible, objective(at:x) == objectiveValue, and a valid bound.

claimsHeld.claim: The baseline gates pass, and Thread Sanitizer finds no data races in branch and bound or its liveness tests.
claimsHeld.howChecked: Read verification/baseline/progress.txt, 03-test-debug.log, 04-test-release-integration-liveness.log and 05-tsan.log. Every step returned rc=0, and the logs contain 0 race reports. Under TSAN, the BranchAndBound suites (26 tests), L1-L10 (24 tests) and MIPLIBCorpusTests passed. The one known issue is mod008 under CP-SAT without the LP propagator.

overflow: info: In a debug build, the MIPLIB branch-and-bound corpus test returns early for slow instances unless ZTRONLP_SLOW_TESTS=1. This is documented in Tests/ZTronLPIntegrationTests/CorpusTests.swift:7-12, and the release run covers those instances.

info: In near-integral families, objectiveValue often differs from objective(at: primal) by about 1e-5 (385 cases in nearint 1..1500). The root cause is the same as B4-01 and B4-02: the LP objective is kept for a rounded point.

info: stein45 took 58.6 s (primal) and 49.6 s (dual), against 16 to 20 s in README §5, under load averages of 89 to 541 on 8 cores. The difference cannot be attributed to the package, so it is not reported as a false claim.
